children: With the merger of Paramount Skydance with Warner Bros. Discovery complete and shares off restriction, J.P. Morgan gives the newly formed Skydance

a Neutral rating and $9 price target ($15 upside from Thursday’s close), weighing the opportunities created by such a large media company against the challenges in maintaining subscribers and the potential for a downturn in the advertising market.
A company of this size, which is larger by revenue than Netflix
and Disney ex-parks

, “creates opportunities to improve content monetization, cross-sell streaming services, and remove duplicated costs,” said analyst David Karnovsky. But with linear as the key earnings contributor and 6.1x 2026e net leverage, Skydance
has “little room for execution missteps or challenges outside the company’s control.”
Karnovsky believes Skydance
can achieve its synergy goal but respects investor skepticism that the company can reach its EBITDA and free cash flow targets.
“We believe the market will need to see evidence that the integration is improving cash generation before becoming more constructive,” Karnovsky notes.
The movie business looks promising with a 2027-2028 pipeline that includes
The Batman Part II,
The Hunt for Gollum, Sonic 4, Man of Tomorrow,
and
Minecraft
, while Karnovsky views the 30-32 film mandate as manageable.
“But the growth plan requires a wide-release output and cadence that only Universal has successfully executed since 2021,”

In streaming, ad-free pricing premiums and bundling are the “real levers” for earnings growth. However, the Disney+ and Hulu bundle underscores the challenges of combining platforms. Moreover, subscriber growth must occur at the same time Netflix
and Disney
are increasing spending on content and acquisition costs.
Since the merger was completed on October 6, shares of Skydance
have been down 18%, with the bulk of the loss occurring after the company issued 470M warrants.

title: Skydance's size creates synergy opportunities but also risks from cord-cutting, bundling -- JP Morgan
